description: Moves or renames a page (another folder, another slug, or both) in one change: its route, its file on template sites (src/pages mirrors the folders, imports follow) and plain HTML sites (<slug>/index.html or <name>.html), every internal link to it in the site's code and CMS items (Link to, a href, the nav and footer), a redirect from the old address when it was published, and the site plan's entry (purpose, notes and SEO move with it). Works on template sites, React sites whose routes are in code with literal paths, and plain HTML sites; the home page and pages with a variable part keep their address (collection pages move with update_collection settings.urlFolder). Refused with 409 and action ask_agent when Xodia can't do it safely (route_shape_unsupported, route_unreadable, html_pages_listed, or relative_links: an HTML page linking its files relative to its folder): then move it in code yourself, update every link and add the redirect (skill redirects). Addresses are lowercase words with dashes, up to 5 folder levels; an address another page, folder or collection uses is refused with address_clash and the reason (a collection's item level, /blog/<slug>, belongs to its items unless the collection reserves that slug). dryRun says what would change first. Where move_page works, never move a page by editing routes or files by hand. Saved at once, like every edit in Xodia; pushing to Git and publishing stay the user's. The site plan follows in the same change.

branch.description: Optional branch; default the branch the workspace has open

dryRun.description: Only say what would change (files, links, redirects); writes nothing

redirect.description: Omit: a redirect from the old address only when the page was published (it was in the last restore point before this change); true: always; false: never

to.description: Its new address ("/company/about"): another folder, another slug, or both

name: move_page
title: Move a page
